metadata.note: ai-explainer / claude-hai. AI Debt Tracker WEEK 3. ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00 (cold open, answered), B09 (verdict artifact), B10 (handoff) and B11 (outro) only — every body beat illustrates its concept as a native animated Remotion scene (REBUILD LAW). The four source PNGs and their SVG sources are REFERENCE in pantry/, never slotted as media. The script's eight sections become eight body beats: 0:15 splits into B01 (the two scores) and B02 (the three named reports), and the closing on-camera section becomes a limits beat. FOUR THINGS NOT TO GET WRONG: the agent still cannot read a filing into facts; 3 of 3 is a calibration and 1 of 3 is the measurement, with 2 drawn reports excluded rather than counted; 24 of 24 recall sits beside 24 of 26 precision and 20 of 24 event types; and the 50 labels are Claude's judgment, not a person's. VERTICAL CUT: every beat re-renders from a <pattern>916 portrait composition — a re-layout, never a crop. The narration mp3s are copied from the 16:9 reel, not regenerated, so the two masters are the same edit.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about teaching my A I debt tracker to find the debt news in S E C filings, with a filing timeline, a triage step and a document server. This is week three of the A I Debt Tracker. The agent still cannot read a filing into structured facts. This week built what finds the filings worth reading.

shot.visual_intent: COLD OPEN LAW: the ask is the week itself — find the news, and prove nothing was lost. Lands ANSWERED.

show.event: The ask types into the Claude composer.

show.at: on 'what finds the filings worth reading'
show.event: The result lands ANSWERED with three output lines.

props.segment: Building the Filing Timeline, Triage and Document Server
props.command: Gather every filing in each quarter's window, throw away the ones that are not about debt, and prove to me that nothing was thrown away that should have been kept. Then make the survivors citable.
output: 593 filings in the windows — 394 decided by rules, 199 asked the model, 184 kept
on 50 filings labelled beforehand, triage found 24 of 24 — and kept 2 it should not have
and on 5 fresh answer-key reports, 1 of 3 gradable ones agreed

beats.narration_text: First, last week's leftovers. Three data problems are fixed, and last week's three test reports now all agree. But I'd read those reports by now, so I graded five fresh ones, once. Two of them had no debt on either side, so there was nothing to grade. Of the three that did, only one agreed.

shot.visual_intent: The 2 reports with nothing to grade are DRAWN as an excluded tail. Scoring 1 of 5 would punish the key for empty reports; dropping them silently would hide a denominator change.

show.event: The first bar fills to 3 of 3.
The fresh bar fills to 1 of 3, with 2 dashed cells beyond its end.

props.sparkLine: Three of three on reports I had read. One of three on reports I had not.
props.title: The answer key, checked on reports nobody had read
props.subtitle: Printed debt tables against the answer key, graded once after last week's fixes
props.excludedNote: The dashed cells are the 2 of 5 drawn reports that had no debt on either side, so there was nothing to grade (Cipher Mining, TeraWulf). They are excluded, not counted as agreements.
props.fixed: Last week's three reports now agree — but they are the reports the fixes were made against, so that score is a calibration, not a measurement.

beats.narration_text: Dell's totals agree exactly. The answer key counted the banks' extra allotment on a Super Micro convertible as a second bond. And Core Scientific's small notes have no due date anywhere in the data. Two new defects, written down for next week, not tuned away against the reports that found them. And one reading mistake was mine.

shot.visual_intent: Named reports with named defects, not a score. The defect ids are on the frame because 'left open' is only checkable if the thing left open has a name.

show.event: Three named reports land, the two disagreements in the accent.
The open-defect block lands beneath them.

props.subtitle: Drawn before reading, graded once

props.open: Fixing them against the reports that found them would turn next week's check into another calibration. One reading mistake in the hand-check was mine — a Super Micro coupon taken from the notes' original terms, which were amended in 2025 — it does not change the verdict; the double-counted allotment alone makes that report disagree. beats.narration_text: Now the agent's first job: finding the news. For every quarter, the timeline gathers each eight K, prospectus and term sheet filed in the window, including the subsidiaries that borrow on a company's behalf. Across the development quarters, that's five hundred and ninety three filings. The window ends at the report the quarter is graded on, so nothing later can get in.

shot.visual_intent: The beat is called the filing TIMELINE, so it is drawn as one. A bar chart of filing types would count the same things and show nothing of what the window is.

show.at: on 'gathers each 8-K, prospectus and term sheet'
show.event: Filings land as ticks inside the window.
The window's right edge is the solid accent rule.

props.sparkLine: A window that closes before the answer is published.
props.title: Every filing in the quarter's window
props.subtitle: 25 AI companies and their borrowing subsidiaries, across the development quarters
props.cutoffLabel: cut-off: the report it is graded on
props.subsNote: A company's debt is often issued by a financing subsidiary, so the subsidiaries that borrow on a company's behalf are included — a filing missed there is a bond missed.
props.source: SOURCE: AI Debt Tracker week3/pool.json ← triage_eval.py pool · figdata.json

beats.narration_text: Most of them aren't about debt at all. Triage sorts them. Five plain rules decide two thirds: a new borrowing item on an eight K, a prospectus selling notes rather than shares, a filing with no debt words at all. Only the doubtful third, a hundred and ninety nine, goes to the small local model, at about three seconds each. A hundred and eighty four are kept.

shot.visual_intent: Four free-standing bars would read as four populations. This is ONE population being narrowed, so every row keeps the full 593 outline and the part that fell away stays visible as the gap.

show.event: Each stage fills inside the same full-width outline.

show.at: on 'a hundred and eighty-four are kept'
show.event: The five rules land as chips beneath.

props.sparkLine: Rules first. The model only sees what the rules could not settle.
props.title: From every filing to the ones about debt
props.subtitle: Each bar is the same 593 filings, narrowed

stages.label: Decided by five rules
stages.note: 66% of them, before any model runs

rules: prospectus covers selling notes, not shares
props.modelNote: The model is asked only about the doubtful 199, and keeps 21 of them. It does not read the filing into facts — that is next week's job. (not in figdata.json — from narration_script.md and the project documents)

beats.narration_text: Does it miss anything? Fifty filings, drawn by a fixed random rule, were labelled against a written definition before triage ran, by Claude, a different model from the one being tested. Triage found all twenty four debt filings; the pass line was ninety five percent. It raised two false alarms. And it kept all twenty two filings that last week's search found announcing a bond change.

shot.visual_intent: Perfect recall is the flattering number, so the two that qualify it sit directly beneath it on the same scale, and the two false alarms are NAMED rather than left as a denominator.

show.event: The recall bar fills past the dashed pass line inside it.
The weaker bars land beneath it and the two alarms are named.

props.sparkLine: It found everything. Look at the three numbers under that one.

props.subtitle: 30 drawn at random, 20 from filings containing debt words

beats.narration_text: Not everything went smoothly. The first run crashed when a model answer got cut off mid sentence, so now an unreadable answer keeps the filing. The check also exposed a bug in last week's search: zero percent was matching inside twenty percent. And eight of the model's twenty one yes answers gave a quote that isn't word for word in what it read.

shot.visual_intent: Three things that went wrong is a confession. Three things that went wrong, each with the change it forced, is a record — so the consequence takes the accent, not the failure.

show.event: Each failure lands with the change it forced beneath it.
The quote-check footnote lands.

props.quoteNote: The quote check compares the first 80 characters of the model's quote with the text it was given. 8 of 21 did not match — which can be a paraphrase rather than an invention, so the filing is still kept and the event reader must re-check every fact.

beats.narration_text: That's why the document server matters. It turns a filing into numbered sentences and table cells, so the agent cites sentence five instead of retyping one and a half billion dollars. And it refuses to open the report the agent will be graded on. Every document goes through the same point in time rule.

shot.visual_intent: The citation is shown resolving — query, id, the actual sentence — so 'cites instead of retyping' is seen rather than claimed.

show.event: The query lands and resolves to s5.
The refusal lands beneath it, in the accent.

props.sparkLine: Cite the sentence. Never retype the number.

beats.narration_text: What this does not show. Twenty four of twenty four is recall on a small set; precision is twenty four of twenty six, and the event type is right on only twenty of twenty four. The labels are a model's judgment, not a person's. And a quote that isn't verbatim may be a paraphrase, not an invention. Next: fix the two new defects, check fresh reports, build the event reader.

shot.visual_intent: Every episode in this series ends on its own limits. Each limit is tied to the claim it narrows, never left as a free-floating caveat list.

beats.narration_text: So: five hundred and ninety three filings gathered per quarter window, two thirds settled by five plain rules, and a small local model asked only about the doubtful third. A hundred and eighty four kept. Checked against fifty filings labelled beforehand, it found every one of the twenty four, kept two it shouldn't have, and got the event type right on twenty. The answer key still has two open defects, and the agent still cannot read a filing.

shot.visual_intent: Judgment beat. The artifact page is the point (ILLUSTRATE LAW carve-out).

show.event: Five findings stagger in, one per spoken clause.

props.artifactTitle: Building the Filing Timeline, Triage and Document Server
props.artifactHeading: What week 3 built, and what it is allowed to claim
artifactLines: The answer key re-checked: last week's 3 now agree, but on 5 reports drawn fresh and graded once, 1 of the 3 with any debt agreed. 2 had nothing to grade. Two new defects, left open.

A timeline that gathers every 8-K, prospectus and term sheet in each quarter's window — 593 filings across the dev quarters, including the subsidiaries that borrow for a company. The window ends at the graded report.
Triage: 394 filings settled by five plain rules, 199 sent to qwen3:4b at a median 3.1s each, 184 kept — 163 by rule and 21 by model.
Checked on 50 filings labelled by Claude before triage ran: 24 of 24 found against a 95% line, 24 of 26 kept are debt, event type right on 20 of 24, and all 22 of last week's announcements survive.

A document server that turns a filing into numbered sentences and cells so the agent cites s5 instead of retyping a number — and refuses the report it will be graded on. Three things broke on the way, and each changed something.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. If you have a filter in front of a model, label a sample by hand before you run it, and write the definition down first. Mine found everything it was supposed to, and still kept two things it shouldn't have.

shot.visual_intent: HANDOFF LAW: a real prompt, read ALOUD verbatim and then discussed. One of exactly two typing beats.

show.event: The prompt types into the composer.

props.segment: Building the Filing Timeline, Triage and Document Server
props.command: Write down, in one paragraph, what counts as a positive for my filter — before looking at any of its output. Then label a random sample against that definition, and report recall AND precision separately. Do not let the filter's own answers influence a single label.
